## Description

<!-- SECTION:DESCRIPTION:BEGIN -->
Reported via opag/ISSUES.md, verified against source 2026-09-02: src/cli/main.ts's task command dispatch (line 1588) only recognizes complete/archive/demote as verbs; there is no task delete path anywhere in main.ts. milestone and decision, by contrast, both have a real delete action (main.ts:1203-1204, 1308) alongside archive. A probe/throwaway task currently has no way to be removed and must be archived instead, which is semantically wrong for a task that was never meant to persist (e.g. a test task) and pollutes archived history with noise. No ratified doc found deciding this asymmetry deliberately -- QCLI-140 only covers milestone archive rationale (retire without destroying), not why task specifically lacks the delete milestone/decision already have.
<!-- SECTION:DESCRIPTION:END -->

## Acceptance Criteria
<!-- AC:BEGIN -->
- [ ] #1 Decide and record whether task delete should exist, mirroring milestone/decision's delete semantics, or whether the asymmetry is intentional and should be documented as such (e.g. tasks are audit-significant in a way milestones/decisions are not)
- [ ] #2 If added, task delete follows the same actor/actor-kind declaration and non-mutating-on-failure pattern as milestone/decision delete
- [ ] #3 If declined, the reason is documented somewhere an agent hitting this gap would find it (command-help.ts task entry, or a guide) so the next report doesn't re-discover the same gap
<!-- AC:END -->

acceptanceCriteria.text: Decide and record whether task delete should exist, mirroring milestone/decision's delete semantics, or whether the asymmetry is intentional and should be documented as such (e.g. tasks are audit-significant in a way milestones/decisions are not)
If added, task delete follows the same actor/actor-kind declaration and non-mutating-on-failure pattern as milestone/decision delete
If declined, the reason is documented somewhere an agent hitting this gap would find it (command-help.ts task entry, or a guide) so the next report doesn't re-discover the same gap

plan: 1. Record the decision as a Quest decision record: task keeps archive-only; the milestone/decision delete asymmetry is intentional because task records are audit-significant in a way the other two are not
2. Document it on the task archive command-help entry, which AC 3 names as where an agent hitting the gap would look, so the next report does not re-discover it
3. Check whether any guide (task-finalization) should carry it too, rather than only the help surface
implementationNotes:
Decision routed to the repository owner rather than inferred. QCLI-164 noted no ratified doc decided the asymmetry, and this repository own CLAUDE.md records the rule for exactly that case: when a contract is silent, say undetermined and route it, do not infer from the neighbouring clause. Reasoning from QCLI-140 milestone rationale or QCLI-245 direction of travel would have been that inference. Owner decided 2026-09-17: keep archive-only.

Recorded as DEC-8. Documented on two surfaces, both named in AC 3: the task archive command-help entry, and the task-finalization guide. The guide previously said "nothing in Quest deletes tasks on its own", which reads as "no AUTOMATIC deletion" rather than "no delete verb, deliberately" -- that wording was the reason the gap could be re-discovered, so it was sharpened rather than left.

Guard added as test/qcli164-task-delete-asymmetry.test.ts, and mutation-tested rather than only run green: reverting the help edit alone reddened exactly the help assertion (2 pass / 1 fail), reverting the guide edit alone reddened exactly the guide assertion (2 pass / 1 fail), both matching the prediction read off the test file beforehand. Localised, so the assertions test the properties they name rather than the files identity.

Incidental finding worth keeping: the manifest name union does not contain "task delete", so a narrowly-typed Set turns the absence assertion into a COMPILE error -- tsc refused the literal on the first run. That is a real second guard, but a guard that cannot execute cannot be seen to fail, so the Set is widened to string and the runtime assertion kept. Both now hold.

bun run check exits 0, 561 tests across 65 files.

AC 2 is deliberately left UNCHECKED, and that is the correct terminal state for it rather than an oversight.

It reads "If added, task delete follows the same actor/actor-kind declaration and non-mutating-on-failure pattern as milestone/decision delete". The decision was to decline, so the antecedent is false and the criterion is vacuously true. Checking it would have been defensible on formal logic and misleading in practice: a later reader seeing 3/3 checked would reasonably infer a delete verb was implemented and its actor handling verified, when no such code exists and nothing was measured.

This repository already carries an open task about exactly this shape (QCLI-298, a --ready absence assertion passing vacuously on an empty list), so checking it here would have been the same error in the tracker that we have filed against our own test suite.

It was in fact checked reflexively along with 1 and 3, then unchecked on re-reading the conditional. Completing with it unresolved is the designed path: task-finalization says completion prints the unresolved items and adds unresolvedAtCompletion, which is a signal to read these notes, not evidence something went wrong.
finalSummary:
Declined, documented, and guarded. quest task stays archive-only; no task delete verb was added, and the asymmetry with milestone/decision is now recorded as intentional rather than left as an unexplained gap that invites re-filing.

The decision itself was routed to the repository owner, not inferred. QCLI-164 observed that no ratified document decided the asymmetry, and CLAUDE.md records the rule for that exact situation: when a contract is silent, say undetermined and route it rather than reasoning from the neighbouring clause. Owner decision 2026-09-17: keep archive-only.

Reasoning, recorded as DEC-8: a task record is audit-significant in a way a milestone or decision record is not -- every write demands an explicit actor, and the record carries history, gateEvents and comments. task archive already provides retire-without-destroying, which is what the motivating case (a throwaway probe task) actually needs. The motivating case is also weaker than it looks: .quest/ is committed to Git, so a deleted record would remain recoverable from history and delete would not deliver the clean removal it appears to promise. Accepted cost: a probe task is archived like any other.

Documented on both surfaces AC 3 names: the task archive command-help entry, and the task-finalization guide. The guide previously read "nothing in Quest deletes tasks on its own", which states behaviour and scans as "no automatic deletion" rather than "no delete verb, deliberately" -- that wording is why the gap was re-discoverable, so it was sharpened rather than merely supplemented.

Verified: test/qcli164-task-delete-asymmetry.test.ts, mutation-tested rather than only run green. Predictions were read off the test file before running. Reverting the help edit alone reddened exactly the help assertion; reverting the guide edit alone reddened exactly the guide assertion; both 2 pass / 1 fail, and full green on restore. Localised, so the assertions exercise the properties they name rather than pinning file identity. bun run check exits 0, 561 tests across 65 files.

AC 2 is left unchecked on purpose -- it is conditional on a delete being added, so it is vacuously true and checking it would imply verification of code that does not exist. See the notes.
